docs.title: High Speed Projection
docs.text:
Design v0.1 · 18 November 2026 · Windows 10/11

HSP listens to a speaker, recognizes a Bible passage, and directs VideoPsalm to display it. VideoPsalm owns the Bible library, slide formatting, and audience output. HSP owns speech capture, command interpretation, session context, validation, and controlled automation.

Design status

This site describes the planned Rust product, not completed Rust functionality. The Python proof of concept supplies integration evidence; each Rust milestone needs its own acceptance test.

docs.title: First milestone
docs.text:
Prove this complete path on a Windows computer with an external display:

Microphone → transcript → structured scripture intent → VideoPsalm search → live projection.

A Type a scripture command field exercises the same intent and projection pipeline without audio. Build the VideoPsalm text-entry path first, then add inference and voice.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
Layer Choice Status Desktop Tauri 2 + React/TypeScript Planned Orchestration Rust + Tokio Planned Audio Rust cpal Planned Streaming recognition ASR adapter; sherpa-onnx is the initial candidate Model/binding selection pending Language interpretation Qwen3-1.7B, non-thinking, on Modal Initial candidate; benchmark required Inference server vLLM; evaluate SGLang after measurement Initial serving choice Desktop control Windows UI Automation / Win32 Port and verify the prototype flow Settings and secrets Local Rust persistence + Windows Credential Manager Planned

The Rust design is network-dependent for language interpretation. Audio/ASR run locally; stable transcript text and bounded context go to Modal. This differs from the Python prototype's local rule-based interpretation. See inference and privacy.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The model interprets language. Rust decides what may execute. Model output never becomes arbitrary keystrokes, shell commands, selectors, or mouse coordinates.

flowchart LR
  subgraph Windows[Windows computer]
    Audio[cpal audio capture] --> ASR[Streaming ASR adapter]
    Text[Typed command] --> Intent[ScriptureIntentClient]
    ASR -->|Stable transcript| Intent
    Intent --> Validate[Validate and resolve context]
    Validate --> Queue[ProjectionCoordinator]
    Queue --> Adapter[VideoPsalmAdapter]
    Adapter --> VP[VideoPsalm]
    VP --> Display[Audience display]
    UI[Tauri and React UI] <--> Queue
  end
  Intent -->|Authenticated HTTPS| Modal[Modal intent service]
  Modal -->|One structured intent| Validate

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Component Responsibility AppOrchestrator / SessionManager Start/stop services, propagate cancellation, publish state AudioCaptureService Enumerate devices, capture frames, meter input, bounded buffering SpeechRecognitionService Stream partial/stable/final segments with timestamps ScriptureIntentClient Authenticated asynchronous requests, deadlines, stale-response rejection ScriptureSession Current passage/translation, last projected passage, history, deduplication ScriptureNavigator Resolve next/previous verse and ranges using canonical metadata TranslationResolver Map recognized names to verified installed VideoPsalm translations VerseSearchService Search a licensed corpus for quotes; return ranked references for review ProjectionCoordinator Validate intents, enforce modes, serialize projection, report results VideoPsalmAdapter Discover/bind controls, search/select, preview/present, observe status SettingsStore Local configuration, Credential Manager access, diagnostic policy React UI Operator controls and state display through Tauri commands/events Modal service Inference only; no desktop or VideoPsalm access

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
src-tauri/src/
  app/          # orchestration, sessions, Tauri commands/events
  audio/        # cpal capture and streaming ASR adapter
  intent/       # Modal HTTP client, wire types, validation
  scripture/    # session, navigation, translations, quote lookup
  projection/   # coordinator, Windows adapter, automation profiles
  settings/     # persistence, credentials, diagnostics
src/            # React/TypeScript UI
inference-modal/# Python service, prompts, model/serving configuration
tests/fixtures/ # labeled utterances, expected intents, adapter traces

This is the proposed application repository layout, separate from this MkDocs repository.

docs.title: Concurrency and cancellation
docs.text:
• Capture callbacks enqueue bounded frames; they do not run ASR, HTTP, or automation.
  • ASR publishes revisions for display. Only sufficiently stable segments enter inference; unstable partial text never projects.
  • Debounce revisions and use a bounded latest-relevant inference queue. Reuse one HTTP client/connection pool.
  • Each session has a cancellation generation. Track request IDs and transcript order; discard responses from an old session, superseded segment, or expired deadline.
  • Run blocking Windows automation on one dedicated, COM-initialized worker. Never block the UI thread or perform competing focus operations.
  • Serialize VideoPsalm transactions. A newer command supersedes older unexecuted automatic commands; cancellation does not undo input already sent.
  • On overflow or excessive lag, discard obsolete work, pause Automatic mode, and show the reason. Buffer sizes, timeouts, and debounce intervals need benchmark-based defaults.

docs.title: Session state
docs.text:
ScriptureSession holds current_reference, current_translation, last_projected_reference, last_intent_id, and bounded history. Keep detected/approved passages distinct from a confirmed live projection. Track context age and its origin so relative commands cannot silently use stale or ambiguous context.

Deduplicate the resolved action/reference/range/translation tuple. A sent-but-unverified command can already be live, so suppress its duplicates too. An operator-requested repeat is explicit.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Disconnected → Connected → Listening → Interpreting → Candidate
Candidate → WaitingApproval → Preparing → Presenting → Result
Candidate → Preparing                       # eligible Automatic only
Any active stage → Stopped / RecoverableError

Stopped means capture and future automation are canceled. It does not mean VideoPsalm's audience display has been blanked or frozen. A hung native call may outlast a Rust deadline; define a worker recovery strategy rather than promising that every call is interruptible.

docs.title: Data and API contracts
docs.text: The shapes below are a proposed v1 implementation contract derived from the design. They are not evidence of a deployed endpoint. Share matching wire types and fixtures between Rust and the Modal service.

docs.title: Domain types
docs.text:
Type Essential fields AudioFrame Samples, channels, sample rate, monotonic capture timestamp TranscriptSegment Segment ID, revision, text, start/end, stable/final flags IntentRequest Request/session IDs, stable text, current passage/translation, recent context ProjectionIntent Action, reference, translation, range, quote, confidence, evidence span, request ID BibleReference Canonical book, chapter, start verse, optional end verse ProjectionCommand Command/request/session IDs, resolved reference/version, mode, creation/deadline, cancellation generation ProjectionResult Command ID, outcome, message, timings, observed selection/live state when available

Use monotonic clocks for durations/deadlines and wall-clock timestamps for human-readable history. Preserve the model response for validation diagnostics only when the operator's privacy policy allows it.

docs.title: Interpret endpoint
docs.text:
POST /v1/interpret over HTTPS, authenticated with a bearer credential held by the Rust client. The service validates authentication before inference. The endpoint URL is configured during setup; none is deployed by this documentation.

Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <credential>

Request example (JSON):

{
  "request_id": "req-0001",
  "session_id": "session-0001",
  "stable_transcript": "Turn to Romans chapter eight verse twenty-eight",
  "current_reference": null,
  "current_translation": "KJV",
  "recent_context": []
}

Response example (JSON):

{
  "request_id": "req-0001",
  "action": "SHOW_REFERENCE",
  "reference": {"book": "Romans", "chapter": 8, "verse": 28},
  "translation": "KJV",
  "verse_range": null,
  "quote": null,
  "confidence": 0.98,
  "evidence_span": "Romans chapter eight verse twenty-eight"
}

reference is an object or null; chapter and verse are positive integers. A same-chapter verse_range is {"start": 28, "end": 30} or null; its start must equal reference.verse. Normalize into the domain reference only after checking consistency and canonical boundaries. Cross-chapter range support must be explicitly added and tested, not inferred from this shape.

translation, quote, and evidence_span are strings or null. Codes are normalized by Rust and mapped to installed translations; missing versions are errors, never silent substitutions. A null translation retains the configured/current version. Confidence is a number in [0,1]: it is model-reported evidence, not a calibrated probability or permission to project.

docs.title: Action rules
docs.text:
Action Required interpretation Rust behavior SHOW_REFERENCE Explicit complete reference; optional same-chapter range/version Normalize, validate, resolve translation, create a command NEXT_VERSE Recent usable reference context Compute the next canonical verse, including chapter/book boundaries PREVIOUS_VERSE Recent usable reference context Compute the previous canonical verse; reject before the Bible's beginning SET_TRANSLATION Recognized translation and recent passage context Resolve an installed version for the current passage SEARCH_QUOTE Non-empty quote; no guessed reference Search the licensed index, show ranked candidates, require candidate selection NONE No actionable scripture request Update transcript/status only

For relative actions, Rust resolves context itself and rejects any conflicting model-supplied reference. Missing/ambiguous context goes to operator review. An incomplete book/chapter mention must not acquire an invented verse.

docs.title: Validation before execution
docs.text:
1. Require a matching request ID and an active, unexpired session/generation.
  2. Deserialize the constrained schema; reject unknown actions/fields, invalid types, missing action-specific data, or malformed references.
  3. Check evidence against the transcript, canonical chapter/verse metadata, range order, context freshness, and installed translation mapping.
  4. Apply deduplication and uncertainty/multiple-reference checks. One model response never authorizes rapid presentation of several passages.
  5. Enforce the selected mode and operator overrides, then enqueue one supported command.

No model field may specify a control selector, executable, keystroke sequence, file path, or arbitrary desktop action.

docs.title: Errors and results
docs.text:
Proposed HTTP errors use {"request_id":"req-0001","error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}: 401/403 authentication, 422 bad input, 429 saturation, and 503/504 unavailable/timed-out inference. A local network error is also visible in HSP. Retry only the latest still-valid interpretation request within its deadline; never blindly retry a presentation whose outcome is unknown.

Projection outcome Meaning CONFIRMED Supported observation verifies the intended live reference and translation SENT_UNVERIFIED Input was sent, but live output could not be independently confirmed FAILED A known step failed; include the step and whether any input was sent CANCELED Work was canceled; report partial dispatch separately if it occurred UNSUPPORTED Required capability, translation, or verified workflow is unavailable SIMULATED Mock execution only; no audience output changed

Emit UI events for connection, audio/ASR state, transcript, candidate, command step, result, and recoverable error. Every command result remains correlated with its IDs and stage timings.

docs.title: Design baseline
docs.text:
This documentation follows HSP Rust Low-Level Design v0.1, 2026-11-18. The Rust/Tauri desktop and Modal-hosted language interpretation are the planned product architecture. The existing Python proof of concept is a separate implementation and source of observed integration behavior.

The added HTTP field shapes, result names, and lifecycle rules make the design implementable; they are proposed contracts, not a claim that code or an endpoint already exists.

docs.title: Open decisions
docs.text: Decision Evidence needed ASR model and Rust binding Streaming English scripture tests, Windows packaging, CPU/latency measurements, licensing Qwen model size and sampling Compare 0.6B, 1.7B, and a larger baseline on labeled church speech vLLM vs SGLang Accuracy, schema validity, warm/cold latency, and concurrency under the same workload GPU/region/warm schedule Actual client-network p50/p95, service windows, and operating cost Confidence/stability/debounce thresholds Calibration and false-projection tests; no arbitrary probability claims Context and queue limits Session tests, stale-response rejection, and measured backlog behavior Canonical metadata and quote corpus Chapter/verse coverage, translation differences, source provenance, and redistribution/indexing rights VideoPsalm support matrix Rust-side two-monitor tests per release, profile, translation, and action Unresponsive automation recovery COM/thread behavior, deadlines, cancellation, and worker/process recovery tests Deployment and retention Actual app/service build scripts, credential lifecycle, transcript/log policy

docs.title: Delivery and acceptance
docs.text: Build in this order. Each milestone needs executable evidence, not only a design or successful input call.

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text: Milestone Deliverable Exit criterion A — VideoPsalm parity Rust Windows adapter + typed-reference harness Reproduce the verified Python search/select/present flow and confirm audience output on two monitors B — Modal interpretation Authenticated endpoint, Qwen3-1.7B serving candidate, shared contracts/fixtures Realistic text becomes valid, contextual intents; accuracy and latency benchmarked C — Voice end to end Microphone + streaming ASR + full pipeline Clear spoken references reach VideoPsalm with Approval; duplicates, lag, and session stop are exercised D — Contextual actions Navigation, translation changes, quote-search candidates Next/previous, range, installed-version switching, and reviewed quote lookup reuse the same command system

docs.title: Development prerequisites
docs.text:
The application targets Windows 10/11; verify architecture and native-library compatibility before pinning releases. Rust development needs the Windows MSVC toolchain, Microsoft C++ build tools, and WebView2; the React frontend also needs a compatible Node.js toolchain. Follow the official Tauri prerequisites and pin the app toolchains/lockfiles when scaffolding it.

Evaluate the streaming ASR Rust/native binding and package its runtime/model assets. sherpa-onnx is a candidate with local recognition support, not yet a selected HSP model or measured latency result. sherpa-onnx documentation.

The Modal service additionally needs its own Python environment, deployment configuration, model weights, GPU allocation, and authentication secret. App build/run/deploy commands belong in the implementation repo once its actual scripts exist. The documentation README provides working MkDocs commands for this repo.

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text:
Layer Required cases Audio/ASR Device selection/unplugging, resampling, bounded buffers, revision stability, silence/noise, long sessions Interpretation Spoken numbers, numbered books, aliases, ranges, incomplete mentions, ordinary numbers, comparisons, quote vs explicit reference Session/navigation Fresh/stale context, chapter/book boundaries, previous at the beginning, unavailable translations HTTP Authentication, malformed output, unknown actions, timeout, saturation, retries, out-of-order and superseded responses Coordinator All modes, dedupe, one serialized transaction, cancel/pause, stale queue replacement, sent-but-unverified outcomes Windows adapter Wrong focus, missing controls, changed handles/version/DPI, minimization, restart, slow UI, multiple instances, privilege mismatch UI/package Small-screen scrolling, visible errors, operator overrides, clean-machine startup and model/runtime provisioning

Use deterministic fake ASR/intent/adapter providers in automated tests. Keep labeled utterances and expected actions in fixtures. Hardware tests remain separate from mock success.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
Record per-request timestamps, settings, model revisions, hardware, network region, and VideoPsalm version. Report p50/p95 for:

  • ASR stabilization: end of the spoken reference to a stable usable segment.
  • Modal round-trip: client send to validated response, including network and serving time.
  • Search/selection: adapter start through matching VideoPsalm selection.
  • End to end: end of speech to independently observed live output.

Include queue time and cold/warm state. If live output cannot be observed, measure command sent latency separately; do not call it confirmed projection latency.

Design targets under tested clear-speech conditions are p50 ≤ 2 s, p95 ≤ 4 s, and ≥ 98% correct reference extraction on a representative labeled benchmark. They are not measured results or guarantees. Define exact-match scoring, ambiguous/no-action negatives, dataset composition, and held-out evaluation before using the accuracy figure as a release claim.

docs.title: Rehearsal and release gate
docs.text:
On a non-live two-display setup, verify a typed passage, a spoken passage, installed translation handling, preview/live separation, duplicate suppression, Stop/override, and recovery from lost focus/network/app restart. Record audience observations independently of input success. Repeat after relevant profile, model, or application changes.

Before live use, require correct observable projection confirmation for the claimed supported path, operator override, and safe error recovery. Any unobservable outcome remains labeled SENT_UNVERIFIED and does not satisfy a confirmed-projection acceptance check. Package the Windows app, native ASR dependencies/models, and operator setup instructions; validate the distribution on a clean target machine.

docs.title: Modal inference
docs.text: The Scripture Intent Service converts stable transcript text plus session context into one constrained projection intent. It does not operate VideoPsalm or return Bible verse text for rendering.

docs.title: Initial configuration
docs.text:
Setting Initial design choice Model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B Execution Non-thinking mode Serving vLLM; compare SGLang after measurements GPU Start with an L4-class candidate; benchmark alternatives Placement Region close to the actual client/church network Warm capacity min_containers=1 during live-service windows Request shape Short prompt, bounded recent context, short output limit Output Schema-constrained JSON; one action Concurrency Low serving concurrency, selected from load tests

The model card documents a hard non-thinking switch through enable_thinking=False in the chat template. Configure the selected server to honor that switch; verify the response does not contain reasoning markup. Pin the model revision and serving/tokenizer versions after benchmarking. Qwen model card.

The design calls for deterministic inference settings; the exact sampling configuration remains a measured decision. Compare Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B, and a larger baseline for extraction accuracy, context handling, and p50/p95 latency before finalizing the model.

docs.title: Serving lifecycle
docs.text:
Preload weights and initialize the inference engine before a service window. Keep connections warm, restrict output length, and measure both warm and cold requests. Keeping a minimum container count trades reduced cold-start exposure for idle resource cost; it is not a latency guarantee. Modal cold-start guidance.

Implement an authenticated HTTPS handler for /v1/interpret. Reject unauthenticated or oversized requests before inference, constrain decoding, validate the response, and return correlated errors. A Modal web function/ASGI app is the hosting mechanism; the HSP bearer authentication contract must be implemented explicitly. Modal web functions.

Deployment source, service-window scheduling, region, model revision, concurrency, token limits, and timeouts are configuration to finalize in the implementation repository. No endpoint or service deployment exists in this docs repository.

docs.title: Streaming policy
docs.text:
1. ASR displays partial hypotheses locally.
  2. Send stable incremental spans after revision debounce; do not repeatedly submit the growing sermon.
  3. Include current reference/translation and bounded recent context. Assign a request ID tied to the session and segment revision.
  4. Discard superseded or late results even if HTTP cancellation did not stop server computation.
  5. Route low-confidence, ambiguous, comparison, and multi-reference utterances to review. Thresholds need labeled benchmark calibration.

A newer inference response never bypasses Rust validation or the serialized projection queue.

docs.title: Network and data boundary
docs.text:
Microphone capture and the proposed ASR adapter run on Windows. Stable transcript text, current passage/translation, and recent text context leave the machine for Modal over authenticated HTTPS. Raw microphone frames are not part of the interpret API.

The setup UI must explain this boundary. Store the credential in Windows Credential Manager, call the service from Rust, and never expose the secret in React state, frontend storage, logs, or diagnostic exports. Do not retain raw audio or full sermon transcripts by default. Define client and service log retention before deployment.

If the network or inference service is unavailable, show a recoverable error and stop new voice-driven projection. Retain local operator control; do not silently switch models or replay a backlog after reconnection. Typed natural-language commands also use Modal. A separately implemented normalized-reference bypass must be explicit and validated, not assumed to exist.

docs.title: Quote lookup
docs.text: SEARCH_QUOTE sends the spoken phrase to VerseSearchService, not directly to projection. Search an indexed, license-checked corpus and present ranked references. The operator chooses a candidate, which becomes a normal SHOW_REFERENCE command. An LLM's guessed verse is not a search result. This is Milestone D work, not a dependency for first-reference projection.

docs.title: Interface and settings
docs.text: Keep the main window focused on a service operator's task. Detailed setup and diagnostics belong on a separate setup page, with scrolling on small screens.

docs.title: Main window
docs.text:
Area Content Connection Connect to VideoPsalm; Connected/Disconnected and capability/setup status Listening Microphone selector, Start Listening, Stop, clear audio/ASR state Speech Latest transcript; distinguish unstable partial text from stable text Scripture Detected passage, active/requested translation, review state Projection Project when a candidate is ready; last command/result and retry guidance Testing One Type a scripture command field using the same intent pipeline

Show Detected/Connected, Selection ready, Command sent, and Projection confirmed as distinct states. Do not imply successful projection from process detection alone. Errors should identify the failed stage and the next useful action.

docs.title: Operator flow
docs.text:
1. Open VideoPsalm and select the intended Bible translation and display setup.
  2. Connect HSP; confirm the selected instance and available capabilities.
  3. Choose the microphone. Complete ASR/model and Modal setup if needed.
  4. Press Start Listening. In the default Approval mode, review the detected passage and press Project.
  5. Confirm the audience output during rehearsal. Stop cancels listening and unexecuted automation; it does not clear VideoPsalm's display.

For the observed 1.29 workflow, projection must already be enabled in VideoPsalm. Future profiles may expose a separately verified presentation action; do not assume a universal toggle or shortcut.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Mode Detection and execution Approval — initial default Detect and queue; the operator authorizes presentation with Project Manual Show detections for review; only an explicit operator action drives automation Automatic — opt-in Execute only a fresh, validated, unambiguous intent through a supported profile/version mapping

Start Listening does not silently switch Approval into Automatic. Confidence alone never enables Automatic execution. Keep Stop, cancel-pending/pause controls, and operator override accessible. Do not replay old automatic commands after recovery.

docs.title: Setup and persistence
docs.text:
Setting Storage/behavior Microphone Device identity and capture settings; handle disappearance/replacement ASR Provider/model location and compatibility; model provisioning is explicit Modal Endpoint URL and service configuration in local settings Credential Windows Credential Manager; accessed only by Rust Translation Preference plus confirmed installed/displayed mapping Automation Versioned VideoPsalm profile and calibrated capabilities Session policy Mode, context expiry, dedupe, inference/command deadlines Diagnostics Retention and optional transcript logging; redacted exports

Store non-secret configuration under the user's application-data directory. No secrets go into source control or frontend persistence. Show permission, model-loading, network/authentication, and automation errors with appropriate retry/setup actions.

docs.title: VideoPsalm integration
docs.text: Treat the private Python prototype as an integration reference, not a public control API. Port its observed behavior and re-test it in Rust on the installed release.

docs.title: Prototype evidence
docs.text:
On the operator's VideoPsalm 1.29 installation, entering Genesis 1:1 in Bible reference search and pressing Enter selected the verse. The operator confirmed that it appeared on the external monitor while VideoPsalm's Project icon was already enabled.

This confirms that interaction under those conditions; it does not prove the Rust adapter, other releases, translation switching, ranges, or every preview/live mode. Activating a window is different from giving keyboard focus to the reference Edit. The prototype encountered that distinction, and its focus guard prevented typing into the wrong control.

Observed identifiers to inspect—not universal selectors:

Control Observed identifier Main form FormMain Reference entry buttonEditSearchBibleReference Active translation searchLookUpEditBibleList Book selection listBoxControlBibleBooks Chapter selection listBoxControlBibleChapters Verse selection listBoxControlBibleVerses Passage/slide sequence gridControlSequence

Reconfirm IDs, native handles, control roles, and keyboard behavior before using them. Custom DevExpress controls may expose native child Edits more reliably than a generic accessibility value setter. Never persist a native handle as permanent identity; rebind after restart and validate ownership before input.

docs.title: Adapter interface
docs.text:
Operation Contract connect() Locate the intended process/window and bind the profile inspect_capabilities() Discover Bible search, selection, preview/live controls, installed translations search_reference(reference) Focus search, enter the normalized reference, await matching results select_passage(reference, translation) Select the matching range/version; reject mismatches preview_selection() Prepare/verify a preview only if it is known not to affect live output present_selection() Execute the verified live-display action or supported existing-project-mode sequence read_status() Report connection, selected passage, and observable preview/live state

Expose unsupported capabilities explicitly. Keep selectors, verified shortcuts, version information, and timeouts in a versioned automation profile, outside business logic.

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
1. Acquire the one command lock; check command age and cancellation generation.
  2. Verify executable/process, window identity, profile compatibility, and control ownership.
  3. Focus the required control and verify actual keyboard focus before text entry.
  4. Clear stale input, enter the normalized reference, and wait for the result/selection change.
  5. Resolve the installed translation and exact verse/range. Read back selection; fail if it differs.
  6. Verify a safe preview if supported. Otherwise retain HSP's internal candidate until presentation is authorized.
  7. Present using the calibrated workflow. For the observed 1.29 route, leave the operator's Project toggle unchanged and use reference entry + Enter.
  8. Read any supported live observation, publish an honest result, and record each step's duration.

In Manual/Approval modes, do not call a search/preview operation automatically unless its effect on the audience display is verified safe. The selected passage or successful keypress alone is not proof of live output: report SENT_UNVERIFIED when necessary.

The vendor keyboard guide documents Ctrl+F search behavior. Treat it as a calibration candidate, not a verified shortcut for this integration. VideoPsalm keyboard controls.

docs.title: Failure and recovery
docs.text: Wrong focus, missing controls, unavailable translations, slow searches, app restart, privilege mismatch, and operator interaction must produce a visible step-specific error. Stop the transaction rather than guessing a coordinate, replacing a translation, or retrying a possibly live command. Reconnect/recalibrate after identity or layout changes.

docs.title: Integration fixtures
docs.text: Keep sanitized fixtures under tests/fixtures/ in the app repo: VideoPsalm version, Windows/DPI/display setup, process/window selectors, installed translation mapping, exact action sequence, step timings, expected/observed selection, and external-display verification. Capture real screenshots only from the tested installation. Include focus-loss, restart, and failure traces; exclude credentials, personal paths, and sermon recordings.
